videos.title: Put your dot on call
videos.summary: An OpenAI engineer demonstrates a bounded incident-response handoff: a persistent dot watches an on-call channel, investigates a 3 a.m. alert, starts a Codex thread and lets the engineer steer from a phone. The short product demonstration is useful for identifying the coordination pattern, but it is not an independent reliability benchmark. This synopsis relies on creator metadata and indexed scene descriptions, not playback.
videos.why_it_matters: Separate alert detection, evidence gathering and code changes, then keep incident ownership and high-impact approvals with the on-call engineer.

videos.title: How To Actually Automate Your Company w Claude (Seriously)
videos.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
videos.summary: Nick Saraev presents a repeatable automation triage: observe real work, inventory tasks, run each candidate ten times, score the outputs, improve weak procedures, package only passing workflows as skills and schedule only low-risk work. His revenue and automation figures are self-reported, and screen capture can expose secrets. The synopsis uses the creator listing plus a chaptered independent summary, not playback.
videos.why_it_matters: Measure repeatability before scheduling automation, protect captured work data and preserve human review for client-facing or high-impact deliverables.

podcasts.title: Predicted: How AI Is Restructuring Social Life with Mona Sloane
podcasts.source: New Books Network — New Books in Sociology
podcasts.summary: Host Pete Kunze interviews sociologist Mona Sloane about treating AI as social infrastructure rather than a detached technological force. They discuss prediction, classification, institutional authority, technological determinism and public agency. A complete indexed transcript grounds the synopsis, while the publisher listing and independent catalog establish identity, date and runtime. The conversation helps leaders examine who defines predictive categories and who can challenge them; audio was not played.
podcasts.why_it_matters: Ask which institutional assumptions an AI workflow encodes, whose authority it changes and what meaningful route exists for affected people to contest predictions.
